stories.title: Gartner: 'Context Graphs Ground AI Agents With Enterprise Knowledge' — 42% of Enterprises Say Agent Costs Now Exceed Value
stories.body: In a report published 15 September 2026, Gartner identifies context graphs as the foundational layer that grounds AI agents in the declarative, procedural, and causal knowledge required to reason about enterprise tasks, with policies enforced through runtime constraints. The firm reports that 42% of enterprises say AI agent costs now exceed value realized, and that only 39% of enterprises currently use knowledge graphs and 36% use ontologies — the two building blocks the report calls prerequisites. Without a context layer, Gartner warns, agents 'operate on stateless logic over stateful data,' making outputs difficult to trust, audit, or scale.
stories.why: This is the single most powerful proof point a Graas seller can put in front of a CIO: Gartner, not a vendor, is saying context infrastructure is the reason agent pilots stall — and fewer than 40% of enterprises have even the basic graph or ontology layer in place. Use it to reframe the conversation from 'which agent should we buy' to 'what context foundation do we have,' which is exactly where Graas lives.

stories.title: McKinsey State of AI 2026: Agent Scaling at Large Enterprises Jumps to 40%, But Only 37% Report Any EBIT Impact
stories.body: McKinsey's 'State of AI in 2026: On the Road to ROI,' published 25 August 2026 and fielded across 1,719 respondents in 97 countries, finds that 40% of organizations with more than $1 billion in revenue are now scaling AI agents in at least one function, up from 27% a year earlier — while smaller organizations stayed flat at 22%. Despite record adoption, only 37% of all respondents report any positive EBIT impact from AI, unchanged from 2025, and just 6% of organizations qualify as high performers attributing meaningful profit to AI. Separately, 32% of organizations have already decided against buying at least one software product because they expect to build the capability with AI instead.
stories.why: The EBIT flatline at 37% is the sharpest counter-narrative to 'AI is working everywhere' and gives a seller an evidence-backed reason why a retailer's current agent pilots are likely stuck in productivity theatre, not P&L impact. The build-vs-buy finding (32% skipping software purchases) is a live budget threat every SaaS vendor — including competitors — needs to address head-on.
stories.source_label: McKinsey & Company — The State of AI 2026

stories.title: BCG Case: Global CPG Leader Shifts Replenishment to Agentic AI, Achieves 2–4% In-Stock Lift and 40–60% Admin Savings
stories.body: BCG's May 2026 Executive Perspectives report on supply chain documents a global CPG company that redesigned replenishment using GenAI-enabled agents to deliver in-stock alerts and smart replenishment recommendations — including DC-to-store transfers and expedited orders — validated through a human-in-the-loop feedback loop. Outcomes reported: a 2–4 percentage-point improvement in in-stock rate driving revenue lift, a 4–10 point improvement in fill rate, and 40–60% reduction in administrative time. The agent architecture was built with a modular back end designed for future expansion across additional supply chain functions.
stories.why: This is a named, outcomes-attached CPG deployment from a top-tier consulting firm — exactly the proof a seller needs when a prospect says 'show me someone like us who has actually done this.' The 40–60% admin savings figure is quotable in a first meeting; the modular back-end framing directly maps to Graas's argument for a governed data foundation before agent expansion.
stories.source_label: BCG Executive Perspectives — Supply Chain: From Copilots to Enterprise (May 2026)

stories.title: Salesforce Closes $3.6B Acquisition of Fin (Formerly Intercom) in September 2026, Folding It Into Agentforce at $1.2B ARR
stories.body: Salesforce completed its acquisition of Fin — the company formerly known as Intercom, which renamed itself in May 2026 — on 10 September 2026 for approximately $3.6 billion. Fin now operates inside Salesforce AI Labs alongside Agentforce, which Salesforce reported at $1.2 billion in annual recurring revenue in its first fiscal quarter of 2027. Fin retains its $0.99-per-outcome pricing and reports a 76% average resolution rate; it now sits in Salesforce's customer-service portfolio beside Agentforce's $2-per-conversation pricing, creating a two-tier offer within a single vendor.
stories.why: For a Graas seller, this consolidation means a direct competitor (Fin) is now bundled inside the Salesforce stack that most enterprise retail and CPG accounts already run — lowering the switching cost for incumbents to expand agent coverage without a new vendor relationship. Understanding how Fin's resolution rate and per-outcome model compares to Graas's context-grounded approach is essential before any Salesforce-heavy prospect call.
stories.source_label: getmacha.com / guptadeepak.com (prices and deal terms verified Oct 2026)

stories.title: Tredence Agentic AI Recovers $6.5M in CPG Trade Deductions Across 30+ Integrated Systems
stories.body: Tredence published details in October 2026 of an agentic AI deduction-management deployment for an enterprise CPG client in which agents integrated across more than 30 systems — including SAP, EDI feeds, retailer portals, and email — to evaluate each deduction, assign reason codes, and recommend next-best actions automatically. The deployment recovered $6.5 million from approximately $40 million in addressable deduction spend for a single enterprise client. The architecture required human approval points for financial exceptions and contractual changes, and the system tracked processing time, exception rate, and document-processing accuracy as primary outcome metrics.
stories.why: Trade deductions are one of the highest-friction, data-intensive workflows in CPG-to-retail operations — and this case shows agents can only work across 30+ systems when there is a governed integration and context layer underneath them. A Graas seller can use this to reframe the deduction use case: the agent is the headline, but the cross-system data fabric is what actually made the $6.5M recovery possible.
